description: Build the Phase-6a off-model engine: a new .apia/scripts/share.py implementing the four LOCAL, git-based capabilities, REUSING the existing functions (no duplication). All deterministic, stdlib + optional PyYAML, NO LLM, NO network. (1) KNOWLEDGE PACKS: versioned export/import of the committed .apia/knowledge/ artifacts (ingest.ARTIFACTS incl. project-facts.md + the .index.json) with a schema_version field and a SAFE merge on import that never silently clobbers a local correction. (2) ORG/TEAM PROFILES: apply a committable profile file that layers onto the existing config.yml structure (review.thresholds, eval_data, generate, orchestrate, token_budget, confidence_threshold, stacks) with a documented precedence where LOCAL config overrides the profile. (3) PLUGIN LOADER: discover team-provided LOCAL plugin files (adapters/scanners/shapes) under a committable .apia/ dir and expose a loader the existing engines consult; graceful (never crashing) on a malformed plugin. (4) CAPABILITY MANIFEST: a machine-readable description of this install (adapters present + complete-vs-stub, scanners available, supported shapes, loaded plugins, versions) REUSING ingest.doctor() + scan/scaffold/verify detection. Wire the plugin loader into ingest/scan/scaffold/verify so a local plugin is actually discovered and used. Add the CLI and real tests. Works for BOTH Python and C++ via the existing stack-adapter abstraction.
steps: Create .apia/scripts/share.py. Module docstring states the HARD CONSTRAINT (off-model, no LLM, no network, strictly local, git-based sharing) mirroring orchestrate.py's docstring.

KNOWLEDGE PACKS: implement export_pack(knowledge_dir, out_path) and import_pack(pack_path, knowledge_dir, options). Export: read the ingest.ARTIFACTS files (the 8 committed knowledge artifacts incl. project-facts.md) + ingest.INDEX_FILE ('.index.json') from the knowledge dir and emit a single versioned pack document with a top-level `schema_version` (e.g. '1'), source repo name, generated_at, and per-artifact content + a content hash. Reuse ingest.default_knowledge_dir() for the default location. Import: validate schema_version (forward/backward aware - a known version imports; an unknown/newer version is reported, not silently applied); write artifacts into the target knowledge dir with a SAFE merge that does NOT clobber a locally-corrected artifact (detect a local modification by comparing the on-disk content/hash against what the pack's index recorded, and when they diverge keep the local copy, record it as a skipped/conflict entry in the result, and surface it - same anti-hallucination respect for user-corrected knowledge). Provide an explicit opt-in override (e.g. options force=True) that is NOT the default. Return a structured result {schema_version, imported:[...], skipped_local:[...], conflicts:[...], unknown_version:bool}.

ORG/TEAM PROFILES: implement load_profile(path) and apply_profile(profile, local_config) returning the EFFECTIVE merged config dict. Precedence: deep-merge the profile UNDER the local config so LOCAL overrides win (local key present -> local wins; absent -> profile fills in). Keep it consistent with the existing config.yml keys (review.thresholds, eval_data, generate.supported_shapes, orchestrate, token_budget, confidence_threshold, stacks); do NOT invent new top-level config concepts. Define the profile file location as a committable file under .apia/ (document the exact path + precedence). Return the merged config plus a provenance map (which keys came from profile vs local) for the manifest/report.

PLUGIN LOADER: implement discover_plugins(repo_path=None) and load_plugins(repo_path=None) that scan a committable plugin directory under .apia/ (define the exact dir, e.g. .apia/plugins/ with adapters/ scanners/ shapes/ subdirs or a documented layout) for LOCAL plugin files only (NO download/fetch/marketplace). An adapter plugin is a YAML consistent with the .apia/adapters/README.md schema; a scanner plugin extends an adapter's scanners: contract; a shape plugin names a new shape id consistent with scaffold's contract. Return a structured catalog {adapters:[...], scanners:[...], shapes:[...], errors:[...]}. A MALFORMED plugin (bad YAML / missing required keys) is captured in `errors` and skipped - the loader NEVER raises. Keep within the no-LLM/no-network invariant.

WIRE the loader into the engines (REUSE, do not fork): make scan.py adapter/stack resolution and ingest stack detection consult discover/load_plugins so a team-provided adapter is found; make scan scanner enumeration pick up a plugin scanner; make scaffold.resolve_supported_shapes include plugin-provided shape ids; make verify.load_adapter path resolution able to find a plugin adapter. Each wiring must be additive and preserve ALL existing behavior when no plugins are present (the plugin dir is optional). Prefer a single shared helper in share.py the engines import, keeping config resolution REPO-FIRST.

CAPABILITY MANIFEST: implement build_manifest(repo_path=None) returning a machine-readable dict: apia version/schema_version; per-adapter {name, present, complete|stub} (complete when the adapter declares the real sections e.g. scanners:/non-null test_command; stub for csharp/groovy); available scanners (REUSE scan.scanner_tools_report / the adapter scanners: enumeration and ingest.doctor() presence); supported shapes (REUSE scaffold.resolve_supported_shapes); loaded plugins (from the loader catalog incl. any errors); and a doctor() preflight summary (REUSE ingest.doctor()). Add format_manifest(manifest) for a compact human string, mirroring ingest.format_doctor_report style. No network.

CLI: add main(argv) with a mutually-exclusive action group --export-pack / --import-pack / --apply-profile / --manifest / --plugins / --doctor and shared options (--repo, --knowledge-dir, --out, --pack, --profile, --force, --json), consistent with the other scripts; __main__ exits with the return code. --doctor reuses ingest.doctor()/format_doctor_report. --json emits the machine-readable structure.

CONFIG: in .apia/config.yml, under existing structures only, add a `share` entry to token_budget if a share stage budget is warranted, and document (as comments consistent with the file's style) the shared-profile file location + precedence and the plugin discovery dir. Do NOT introduce a parallel config system; keep all existing keys intact.

COMMITTABLE EXAMPLES: add a tiny example org/team profile file and a tiny example LOCAL plugin (an adapter and a scanner, and a shape if feasible) under the documented .apia/ locations so the mechanism is demonstrable and testable, each clearly labeled as an example.

TESTS: create .apia/scripts/tests/test_share.py with REAL tests: (a) knowledge-pack export->import ROUND-TRIP asserting the imported artifacts + project-facts match the source exactly; (b) SAFE-MERGE: a locally-corrected artifact is NOT silently clobbered by import (asserted via the skipped/conflict result and the on-disk content unchanged), and force=True does override; (c) version-field handling: a known schema_version imports, an unknown/newer version is reported not applied; (d) profile apply + PRECEDENCE: profile values apply where local is absent, LOCAL override wins where present; (e) PLUGIN discovery/load for at least one adapter AND one scanner (and a shape if feasible), asserting the relevant engine (ingest/scan/scaffold/verify) actually discovers+uses it; (f) a MALFORMED-plugin graceful-failure case (captured in errors, loader does not raise, engines still work); (g) CAPABILITY-MANIFEST content: python complete, cpp complete, csharp/groovy stub, available scanners, supported shapes, loaded plugins, versions present; (h) the no-LLM/no-network static guard test for share.py mirroring the existing tripwire lists. Exercise Python and C++ contexts where relevant. Extend test_ingest.py/test_scan.py/test_scaffold.py/test_verify.py minimally to assert plugin discovery in each engine if that is where the wiring lives.
Keep ALL 296 existing tests unchanged and green.
acceptance_criteria: `py_compile .apia/scripts/share.py` is clean and the module imports with stdlib + optional PyYAML only.
share.py --manifest --json on the APIA repo reports python=complete, cpp=complete, csharp=stub, groovy=stub, lists scanners, supported shapes, loaded plugins (incl. the example plugin), and versions.

A knowledge pack exported from an ingested sample and imported into a fresh knowledge dir yields byte-identical artifacts + project-facts; a locally-corrected artifact is preserved (reported skipped/conflict) unless --force is given.
Applying the example org profile produces an effective config where profile values fill absent keys and local config overrides win where present.
ingest/scan/scaffold/verify discover and use the example local plugin; a malformed plugin is captured as an error and does not crash any engine.
The full pytest suite passes: 296 existing + the new share tests, 0 failed, with the extended timeout.
The new no-LLM/no-network guard test for share.py passes.
verification: .venv/bin/python -m pytest .apia/scripts/tests/ -q  (timeout >= 600000 ms) -> all green incl. new share tests
findings:
DONE. New off-model engine .apia/scripts/share.py implements all four Phase-6a LOCAL git-based capabilities, REUSING existing functions (no duplication): (1) KNOWLEDGE PACKS export_pack/import_pack with schema_version '1', per-artifact content+hash, safe no-clobber merge (divergent local copy kept + reported in conflicts/skipped_local; force=True overrides via `forced`), unknown/newer version reported not applied; reuses ingest.ARTIFACTS/INDEX_FILE/default_knowledge_dir. (2) ORG/TEAM PROFILES load_profile/apply_profile + effective_config: deep-merge profile UNDER local config so LOCAL wins, with a provenance map; profile file = .apia/profile.yml (example at .apia/profiles/example-team.yml). (3) PLUGIN LOADER discover_plugins/load_plugins under .apia/plugins/{adapters,scanners,shapes}/ (REPO-FIRST, deduped by realpath so the APIA repo itself is not double-scanned); malformed plugins captured in `errors` (caught yaml.YAMLError), never raises; shared helpers plugin_adapter_path/plugin_scanner_defs/plugin_shape_ids imported by the engines. (4) CAPABILITY MANIFEST build_manifest/format_manifest reusing ingest.doctor + scan.load_adapter/_adapter_path_for_stack/scanner_tools_report + scaffold.resolve_supported_shapes.

WIRING (all additive, preserve existing behavior when no plugins present): scaffold.resolve_supported_shapes appends plugin shape ids; scan._adapter_path_for_stack falls back to plugin adapters; scan.scan() folds plugin scanner defs (keyed on adapter.name) into enumeration and StubAdapterError now also accounts for plugin scanners; ingest.detect_stacks surfaces a plugin stack when its declared extensions/manifests have repo evidence (marked plugin=True); verify.resolve_adapter_path + load_adapter(repo_path=) resolve a bare stack name to a plugin adapter. No import cycle despite ingest<->share (top-level imports only, verified).

CONFIG: added token_budget.share: 2000 and a documented comment block (profile location+precedence, plugin dir) under existing structures only. Adapters README extended with the Phase-6a plugin/extension contract. Example profile + example adapter(lua)/scanner(radon-mi)/shape(cpp_plugin) plugins committed under .apia/.

TESTS: new test_share.py (21 tests): pack round-trip byte-identical incl project-facts, safe-merge preserve + force override, identical-not-conflict, known/unknown version handling, profile precedence (unit + shipped example), plugin discover/load, scaffold/scan/verify/ingest engine discovery+use, scan runs a plugin scanner for real, malformed-plugin graceful failure, manifest completeness (python/cpp complete, csharp/groovy stub) + scanners + shapes + plugins + versions + C++ context, and the no-network/no-LLM guard. Minimal plugin-wiring tests also added to test_ingest.py/test_scan.py/test_scaffold.py (no test_verify.py exists; verify wiring covered in test_share.py).

Did NOT commit (orchestrator handles commits/PR). Nothing was non-executable.
review_fixes: Post-review cleanup pass (review-v1, APPROVED, 4 findings). FIXED 1,2,3; JUSTIFIED+documented 4. (1) EXIT-CODE CONTRACT [fixed, doc]: made the contract self-consistent by choosing the intended design -- a preserved local correction is a SUCCESS (exit 0), conflicts surfaced in the report/--json (conflicts+skipped_local), non-zero ONLY on an unknown/newer schema_version where nothing was applied. Corrected the misleading module docstring line ('Exit 0 ... non-zero otherwise') and the import_pack docstring, and added an explaining comment at the CLI --import-pack return. Behavior was already exit-0; the mismatch was the docs, so no behavior change. Added tests test_cli_import_exit_zero_even_with_preserved_correction and test_cli_import_exit_nonzero_only_on_unknown_version. (2) INDEX OVERWRITE ON ALL-CONFLICT IMPORT [fixed, behavior]: gated the index write in import_pack on at least one artifact actually being applied (wrote_from_pack via a real write/force, OR a pure re-import where every artifact was byte-identical). An all-conflict import (every artifact a preserved local correction, nothing written) now leaves any existing local .index.json UNTOUCHED, so the on-disk index never describes unapplied pack content. (Note: the index is ingest's {source_path:hash} oracle, NOT keyed by artifact filename, so a per-name merge-filter would wrongly empty it; the gate is the correct fix.) Added tests test_all_conflict_import_does_not_overwrite_local_index (asserts imported==[], index_written False, divergent local index survives byte-for-byte) and test_index_written_when_at_least_one_artifact_applied. (3) verify.py DIRECT TEST [fixed]: added .apia/scripts/tests/test_verify.py (8 tests) covering resolve_adapter_path + load_adapter directly for BOTH the bare-stack-name plugin resolution AND the unchanged file-path / python-default-fallback paths (existing file returned as-is, unknown name returned unchanged -> python default, empty no-op, never-raises on a bad repo). (4) SCAN `tools` ASYMMETRY [justified, documented]: DECISION = intended, leave as-is. The `tools` block is the stable doctor-style presence advisory for the ADAPTER-DECLARED scanner contract; a folded-in plugin scanner is already reported in the per-run `scanners` metas and in the manifest scanner union (share.build_manifest). Making `tools` adapter-only keeps the adapter's advertised toolset from shifting with whatever plugins a repo happens to ship. Added a one-line NOTE comment in scan.scan documenting this. VERIFICATION of fixes: py_compile clean; full suite 331 passed, 2 skipped in ~258s (was 319+2; +12 new tests: 4 share + 8 verify); the 2 skips remain the cppcheck-absent conditional skips; no-LLM/no-network guard test for share.py intact and passing.
